findings.claim: The seam-straddling device 'the daughters quoting the oath root back at MT 5:9' is disclosed on both sides of the P02-002/P02-003 seam with an incompatible Hebrew citation: P02-002 names the wrong token as bearing the oath root.
findings.evidence: P02-002 (span Song.5.2-Song.5.8) device_notes (verbatim): "...at the back seam, שֶׁכָּ֖כָה (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) repeats the oath root immediately across this row's own closing verse, the daughters quoting it back — the same-root site the four-site adjuration count excludes on speech-role grounds." MT 5:9's full byte text (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, never hand-typed): "מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ". The final two tokens are שֶׁכָּ֖כָה ('that thus' -- relative-particle + adverb, root כ-כ-ה, no ש-ב-ע consonants at all) then הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ ('you have adjured us' -- the actual oath-root verb, ש-ב-ע). P02-002 cites the WRONG token (שֶׁכָּ֖כָה) as the oath-root repeater. P02-003 (span Song.5.9-Song.5.9) boundary_rationale correctly identifies the real token on the same seam (verbatim): "...That same oath root crosses the row's own front seam: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) is the adjuration and הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) is the daughters quoting it back (skeleton sweep: 5 verses, oath-only root, speech role named on each side)..." The two rows disclose the identical straddling device with two different, mutually incompatible Hebrew citations -- one of them byte-wrong.

findings.claim: The same MT 5:9 straddling device (oath root quoted back) is tagged with two different dotted observed_substrate_signals keys across the two rows that share the seam -- a taxonomy-naming drift for one shared object.
findings.evidence: P02-002 observed_substrate_signals includes "adjuration_refrain.oath_root_quoted_back_5_9"; P02-003 observed_substrate_signals includes "adjuration_refrain.oath_root_quoted_back" (no verse suffix). findings.claim: P02-012 mislabels the MT 7:10-7:14 dod-lexeme recurrence chain as a 'dodi-exact...that exact form' 5-verse chain, but the same chain (correctly named by neighbor P02-013 as 'any attested spelling') necessarily includes MT 7:13's defective-spelling token -- the exact 'dod digit-blending' hazard the toolkit names for this book.
findings.evidence: P02-012 (span Song.7.7-Song.7.9) strongest_rejected_alternative (verbatim): "...even though the dodi-exact token recurs there as part of a five-verse skeleton-tier chain of that exact form (skeleton sweep: 5 verses) reaching across the seam." P02-013 (span Song.7.10-Song.7.10) device_notes/boundary_rationale names the SAME chain differently (verbatim): "A dod-lexeme chain runs across both seams without interrupting either: verses carrying a dod-lexeme token of any attested spelling form 5 consecutive MT verses, MT 7:10-7:14 (= web:Song.7.9-7.13)..." -- 'any attested spelling', not 'that exact form'. P02-014 (span Song.7.11-Song.8.3), which owns MT 7:13 inside that same range, independently confirms the MT 7:13 token is NOT the exact form (verbatim): "...her own 1cs offer, דֹּדַ֖י (oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12, byte tier) 'my love' — the defective spelling of the possessive she offers TO him, not a 2ms form, the single member of the defective-spelling set (sweep: 4 verses) whose suffix runs the opposite direction from the other three." A 5-verse chain spanning MT 7:10-7:14 therefore cannot honestly be labeled 'dodi-exact...that exact form' by P02-012 while P02-014 itself, on the same range, discloses one of its members as the DEFECTIVE (non-exact) spelling -- TOOLKIT.md's SWEEP HAZARD CATALOG names this precisely: 'dod digit-blending (THE Song trap): dodi-exact 24 verses vs dod-family 28 verses vs...the DEFECTIVE דדיך/דדי 4 verses... Name the object, then count.'
